accepted.label: One-Hot Encoding Definition
accepted.description: One-hot encoding represents each word as a sparse vector with a 1 at the vocabulary index and zeros elsewhere, resulting in high-dimensional, inefficient representations.
coverage_criteria: Create a one-hot vector for a given word from a small vocabulary.
Explain why one-hot vectors are sparse and high-dimensional.
accepted.merge_rationale: This candidate stands alone as the fundamental definition of one-hot encoding for words.

accepted.label: One-Hot Encoding Implementation and Comparison
accepted.description: One-hot encoding implementation and analysis, including producing one-hot vectors, explaining the dimensionality problem, and comparing one-hot encoding to dense embeddings.
coverage_criteria: Produce a one-hot vector for a word from a given vocabulary.
Explain the dimensionality problem with one-hot encoding for large vocabularies.
Compare one-hot encoding to dense embeddings.
accepted.merge_rationale: This candidate covers a deeper understanding, including implementation and comparison to dense embeddings, making it a separate concept from the basic definition.
